about: Generic repository decision questions. A verdict informs an operator but never authorizes an action.

instructions.question: Does the defect in `finding` already exist in `base_code`, before the change in `diff`?
instructions.note: Judge the base code as given. A defect the change only moved, renamed or made easier to see is pre-existing; a defect the change created is not.

criteria.true: The base code already has the defect, so the change only moved, renamed or exposed it.
criteria.false: The base code does not have the defect: the change introduced it.

instructions.question: Can exactly one of the alternatives in `alternatives` be the right answer to the decision in `decision`?
instructions.note: Judge the alternatives against each other. Two that could both be taken, or one that contains another, cannot be told apart by a single choice. `alternatives` holds the real options only; leave the no-match option out, because it overlaps every other one by construction.

criteria.true: Taking one option rules out every other one, and no option is a special case of another.
criteria.false: Two options could both be taken, one option contains another, or the same situation satisfies more than one.

instructions.question: Does the evidence in `evidence` prove the acceptance criterion in `criterion`?
instructions.note: Proof is an observed result: a command with its output, a runtime readback, a measured number. A description of what was implemented, a passing unrelated check, a structural assertion about a file, or a plan to run something later is not proof of a behavioural criterion.

criteria.true: The evidence is an observed result, and reading it answers the exact question the criterion asks.
criteria.false: The evidence describes the work instead of showing a result, answers a different question, or was not actually run.
